items.title: Ken Peplowski interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I really learned from a master of that kind of thing, Sonny Stitt, the great saxophone player. I studied with him, I used to watch him play all the time.

ctx.x: So being able to deal with those kind of situations is almost as important as the kind of player you are, because even if you’re a great player, you have to have the ability to be flexible.

You do. And you have to have the ability to not let things phase you that easily. I really learned from a master of that kind of thing, Sonny Stitt, the great saxophone player. I studied with him, I used to watch him play all the time. He did that his whole life. He just traveled around and played with local rhythm sections. And he learned to have a certain consistency in his playing no matter what else was going on behind him. And there’s a talent to that. It teaches you a discipline as a musician. If you can…
Do you book your own things into Spain, and those kind of tours?
